calls.head: A shadow job for Smith, Frondell and Teräväinen
calls.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Frondell’s line (Smith, Frondell and Teräväinen) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Blue Jackets’ first line is Knies, Bel Belluz and Johnson.

calls.head: The Blue Jackets hound the puck, the Blackhawks sit back
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, Columbus is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Blue Jackets to win more pucks back deep in the Blackhawks’ end.

surprises.head: Columbus’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Columbus has a weaker power play than most. Not tonight: 16.9 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.0 and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Columbus brought the hits
surprises.body: Columbus’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 159, against their usual 99 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Knies has a goal and two assists as the Blue Jackets beat the Blackhawks
paras: Zach Werenski got the scoring started for the Blue Jackets just under two minutes in, and Kent Johnson made it 2-0 late in the first. Frank Nazar got the Blackhawks on the board on the power play midway through the second, his fourth straight game with a goal. Matthew Knies stretched the lead to 3-1 on the power play just under two minutes later, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Cole Smith pulled the Hawks within one early in the third, and Adam Fantilli ended any hope of a comeback with an empty-netter with 31 seconds left. Knies finished with a goal and two assists.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Cam Talbot made 23 saves for the Blue Jackets, and Spencer Knight stopped 29 of 32 at the other end. The Blue Jackets improved to 8-12-0 and climbed off the bottom of the Metropolitan to seventh, while the Blackhawks fell to 6-14-2, still last in the Central.

items.text: The Blue Jackets won for the first time in six games.
Zach Werenski extended his point streak against Chicago to seven games.
The Blue Jackets have beaten the Blackhawks seven straight times, going back to the 2023-24 season.
The Blackhawks have won two of their last ten.
